about.title: Port Hueneme Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Port Hueneme residents rely on a small network of local clinics and nearby Ventura County hospitals for everything from routine care to emergency treatment. Most visits go fine, but when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is dosed wrong, or a surgical step is skipped, the harm can be serious and lasting. California treats medical malpractice differently than a typical injury claim — it falls under MICRA, a set of rules unique to healthcare cases that shapes deadlines, damages, and what evidence you'll need. If you believe a provider's care fell below the accepted standard and caused you harm, we can review your medical records and explain your options under these rules. There's no charge to talk, and no obligation to move forward. Given how tight the notice and filing windows can be, reaching out sooner rather than later gives us more room to evaluate your case and build your claim.

whyChoose.title: What Makes Medical Malpractice Cases Different

items.title: Notice Must Come Before the Lawsuit
items.desc: California generally requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the healthcare provider before a malpractice case can be filed. We can help make sure this step happens correctly and on time.

items.title: The Clock Runs Differently Here
items.desc: Medical malpractice claims generally must be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years from the injury itself. Missing either deadline can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Damages and Proof Have Their Own Rules
items.desc: California caps non-economic damages in these cases, though the cap rises each year, and a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to show the care fell below the accepted standard. A bad medical outcome by itself isn't enough — the case has to show an actual departure from that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit, which can affect your timeline. We can look at your specific dates and figure out where you stand.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment in Port Hueneme — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. We can review your medical records to help determine whether the treatment itself was the problem.

items.question: Do I need a medical expert to have a valid claim?
items.answer: Almost always, yes — California malpractice cases typically require a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care wasn't met. This is one of the reasons these cases differ from a typical injury claim. Our team works with the right experts to evaluate your situation.
